approval_required_for: Selection of explicit atol, rtol, and max_mismatch_fraction values and issuance of a new immutable numeric-policy/verification contract; the current role must not invent or relax them.
Reissuing any immutable Stage6 checkpoint, stimulus, target-reference, numeric-policy, or semantic-testbench identity if actual artifact hashes cannot be reconciled to the current contract.

Any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, or major trusted-template change needed because the existing templates lack loader, fallback-guard, or consumption-instrumentation binding hooks. Free-form RTL generation remains excluded from this role.

consumes: artifact.stage7.verification_result as contamination-barred planning/debug evidence only
executable_actions.on_failure: Mark unsupported deltas as out of bounds and route them to the repair boundary auditor for backtrack or approval. Do not generate free-form RTL, change immutable identities, or alter numeric comparison policy.
executable_actions.rationale: Resolve the visible defects into exact existing-template parameter, manifest, loader, fallback-guard, and harness deltas while checking whether the supplied trusted templates expose every required hook. Presence of the template artifacts is established, but the compact prompt does not expose detailed hook coverage, so checker evidence is required.

consumes: artifact.stage7.verification_result as contamination-barred failure evidence only
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep semantic-testbench readiness, operator-leaf functional execution, and Stage7 promotion blocked. Do not insert default tolerances, copy values from another model, or loosen comparison criteria.
produces: approved Stage6 numeric-policy refinement and reissued immutable identity contracts only if approval is granted
executable_actions.rationale: The visible failure explicitly reports missing atol, rtol, and max_mismatch_fraction. This is a policy-level gap, not a template-binding value that this specialist may choose. SACG memory currently has no open backtrack request for this gap, so a bounded approved Stage6 backtrack must be created before a ready semantic harness can bind the values.

consumes: verification/real_weights/full_tensor_catalog.json or a newly generated complete catalog from the same immutable checkpoint
executable_actions.on_failure: Do not copy expected hashes into the manifest or mark it pass manually. If actual checkpoint/reference bytes differ, request contract backtrack; if required loader or guard hooks are absent from trusted templates, classify the repair as a major-template gap requiring approval rather than emitting RTL.
executable_actions.rationale: Use existing code-generation bindings to restore the canonical manifest path and checker-owned status; set accelerator_scope to transformer_blocks_only; derive source_checkpoint_sha256 and source_reference_sha256 from the actual immutable artifacts; bind the exact required current-scope tensor set, including all 12 tensors reported missing by the visible operator-leaf diagnostics; and fail closed on absent, default, identity, sampled, synthetic, or hash-mismatched weights. The complete checkpoint catalog must remain distinct from DUT coverage: model-tail tensors may be cataloged but embedding/tokenization, final norm, LM head/logits, and sampling must be excluded from DUT requirements.

consumes: approved and reissued immutable numeric-policy contract with explicit tolerances
immutable target-model reference manifest produced by real target-model inference on the same checkpoint and stimulus
executable_actions.on_failure: Leave the semantic testbench status incomplete and block the Stage7 retry. Never generate expected outputs randomly, derive them from RTL, use an identity/default target model, alter the golden, or change the immutable tolerance. If generated testbench hashes conflict with the immutable contract, request contract reissuance instead of rewriting expected hashes.
executable_actions.rationale: Generate only trusted-template harness and glue bindings. The manifest must explicitly bind target_model_inference, the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, the independent target-reference hash, dut_weight_binding, numeric_policy_sha256, approved atol/rtol/max_mismatch_fraction, generated source hashes, fail-closed weight loading, and per-required-tensor consumption instrumentation. This action prepares proof instrumentation; only later executed DUT evidence can prove consumption.

executable_actions.on_failure: Return only the failing template, parameter, hash, manifest, fallback, tensor-coverage, or harness binding slice to bounded repair. Keep the numeric policy and golden identities fixed and do not infer a hardware-value failure from a precondition failure.
executable_actions.rationale: Provide checker-ready evidence to repair.repair_boundary_auditor without claiming hardware correctness. These checks must establish complete required tensor hashes, immutable source identity, transformer-block-only scope, fail-closed loading, and a bound semantic harness before any same-layer functional retry is considered.

consumes: sacg_memory_truth active contamination barriers contamination_barrier.0001 through contamination_barrier.0003
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the three Stage7 artifacts contamination-barred and retry_request.0001 open. Do not reuse historical promotion certificates or advance to the connected single-layer or board-wrapped layers.
executable_actions.rationale: The active barriers prevent artifact.stage7.verification_result, artifact.stage7.real_tool_results, and artifact.stage7.debug_closure from being consumed as validated evidence. They do not prevent creation and audit of new Stage8 candidate repairs, but the repair boundary auditor must require approved numeric policy plus all current-stage checker passes before routing a fresh operator-leaf retry. Actual weight-consumption proof and semantic comparison remain Stage7 execution responsibilities.

observations: The visible failure is a semantic-verification precondition and binding failure, not a demonstrated RTL value, order, liveness, or protocol mismatch. Operator-leaf functional simulation, golden comparison, and semantic aggregation were dependency-blocked and did not execute.

The authoritative state summary lists three active contamination barriers on artifact.stage7.verification_result, artifact.stage7.real_tool_results, and artifact.stage7.debug_closure, plus open retry_request.0001 for Stage7. Those artifacts may inform repair planning only and cannot substantiate a pass.

There is no open SACG backtrack request. Because explicit atol, rtol, and max_mismatch_fraction are absent, a new human-approved Stage6 numeric-policy backtrack is required; this specialist cannot fill those fields.

The prompt slice establishes that the template library, template metadata, parameter binding, generated package, memory layout, and case adapter exist. Their detailed rows are omitted, so missing template hooks must not be inferred; template_coverage_check must determine whether the required loader, guard, and instrumentation bindings already exist.

Canonical weight-manifest path/status repair, transformer_blocks_only scope binding, actual-source checkpoint/reference hash reconciliation, exact required tensor entries, fail-closed fallback configuration, and loader/harness references are binding-level defects suitable for bounded_template_repair when existing trusted template hooks cover them.

Immutable hash reconciliation must regenerate or bind artifacts from the actual Stage6 identities and then hash those bytes. Merely copying source_checkpoint_sha256 or source_reference_sha256 expected values into a manifest would conceal contamination and is not an acceptable repair.

A complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog and complete DUT tensor coverage are related but distinct. The catalog must cover the checkpoint; DUT coverage must include every tensor required by the Transformer-block scope, including all 12 current-scope tensors identified by the visible diagnostics, while excluding embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling.

Default, identity, synthetic, sampled-weight, or missing-file fallback paths must fail closed. Disabling such paths is template-bounded only when exposed by existing parameters or trusted loader/harness templates; otherwise it is a major-template gap, not permission for free-form RTL generation.

A manifest and tensor hashes do not prove consumption. Existing-template loader and harness instrumentation can prepare per-tensor load/read evidence, but proof requires later executed DUT evidence showing that every required bound tensor was loaded and consumed through the mapped interface.

The semantic harness can be repaired by binding the target-model inference reference, immutable stimulus, DUT weight manifest, numeric-policy hash, approved tolerance, and generated source hashes. Expected outputs must remain outputs of the real target model on the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, never random data, RTL-derived output, or an identity/default implementation.

Cross-layer memory consistency remains checker-relevant: tensor names, shapes, dtype/precision, packing, data order, offsets, lengths, and addresses must agree across parameter binding, Stage5 memory layout, generated loader, runtime-visible image, and DUT read behavior.

Historical operator-leaf or single-layer outcomes cannot be used to bypass the failed current operator-leaf closure. After repair, the hierarchy must restart at operator/leaf execution; only a fresh pass may permit the connected single-transformer-layer stage.

Board wrapper facts are not implicated by the current operator-leaf precondition failure. Any later board-level retry must preserve the exact user sample-project wrapper and source hashes and must not substitute a simplified AXI/DDR shell.
proposed_actions: Classify only existing-template and parameter-binding deltas, and reject any proposed free-form RTL or numeric-policy edit.
Create a human-approved Stage6 backtrack request for explicit immutable atol, rtol, and max_mismatch_fraction before declaring the semantic harness ready.

Regenerate the canonical DUT weight-binding package from the immutable checkpoint and reference identities, with transformer-block-only coverage, all required tensor hashes, and fail-closed fallback guards.
Generate the semantic harness from trusted templates, binding the same immutable stimulus and independent target-model reference and emitting loader/consumption instrumentation requirements.
Run the declared template, parameter, codegen, hash, real-weight-artifact, and semantic-testbench acceptance checkers; do not manually set pass status.

Hand the checker reports to repair.repair_boundary_auditor while preserving the active Stage7 contamination barriers. If accepted, the verification executor—not this specialist—must rerun the operator-leaf layer and obtain actual consumption and numeric-comparison evidence before any higher-layer promotion.
risks: Numeric comparison cannot pass under the current contract because explicit tolerance fields are absent; any locally invented value would contaminate the golden policy.
Copying expected checkpoint/reference hashes into the manifest without hashing the actual bound artifacts could make a wrong-checkpoint package appear consistent.

Including model-tail tensors in DUT coverage or golden boundaries would violate the Transformer-block-only accelerator scope; omitting any required Transformer-block tensor would leave coverage incomplete.
A complete catalog, manifest existence, or memory image alone can be mistaken for consumption proof unless executed loader/DUT read evidence is required for every bound tensor.
Loader packing, tensor order, offset, length, address, dtype, or shape disagreement with Stage5 memory layout can survive manifest-only checks and produce a later value failure.

If fallback disabling or per-tensor instrumentation is not exposed by the trusted template library, attempting to patch RTL would exceed this role and require a major-template or architecture decision.
Regenerating semantic-testbench sources may change hashes. Any conflict with immutable Stage6 testbench identities requires controlled contract reissuance, not silent hash replacement.
Using contamination-barred Stage7 artifacts or historical promotion certificates as validated evidence could improperly skip the operator-leaf layer.
Board-level work performed later against a substitute wrapper would invalidate deployment evidence even if the current binding repair succeeds.

edges: complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog -> transformer-block-only required tensor projection -> generated/memory/dut_weight_binding_manifest.json
artifact.stage4.parameter_binding + artifact.stage5.memory_layout -> loader shape/order/packing/address bindings -> DUT consumption instrumentation
immutable checkpoint + immutable stimulus -> independent target-model inference -> expected Transformer-block boundary outputs
approved immutable numeric policy -> semantic harness comparison fields; current edge blocked by missing atol/rtol/max_mismatch_fraction
Stage8 checker reports -> repair.repair_boundary_auditor -> fresh operator-leaf Stage7 retry decision
active contamination barriers -> prohibit validated downstream consumption of rejected Stage7 artifacts
nodes: Stage7 contamination barrier and retry node

Actual weight consumption still requires later executed DUT evidence. Missing numeric tolerances are not repairable by this role and require an approved Stage6 contract backtrack. Free-form RTL generation, golden modification, tolerance invention, and use of contamination-barred Stage7 results are excluded.
